title: Finite closed fibre of a purely inseparable integral closure
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $K$ its fraction field, and $L/K$ a finite purely inseparable field extension [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] in characteristic a prime $p$. Let $x\in R$ and suppose $R/xR$ is a domain and N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]. Writing $S$ for the integral closure [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] of $R$ in $L$, the module $S/xS$ is finite [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] over $R/xR$. No completeness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Use Mathlib IsPurelyInseparable.hasExponent_of_finiteDimensional and exponent_def' to choose a common exponent q=p^e. In the algebraic closure of L choose a q-th root z of x. Set E=L(z). The root is integral over L, so the finite-adjoin lemma and field-degree multiplicativity give E finite over K. The preimage of the image of K under the q-th-power Frobenius is a subfield containing L and z. Consequently E^q lies in K. The root is integral over R by IsIntegral.of_pow, giving y in T=integralClosure R E with y^q=x. This construction also works for x=0.

proof.text: Apply tate_root_closure_quotient_finite to E, the same exponent, and y. It gives that T/yT is finite over R.

proof.text: Prove by induction that T/y^nT is finite over R. The n=0 quotient is zero. For the successor step, multiplication by y and the quotient projection form an exact sequence T/y^nT -> T/y^(n+1)T -> T/yT -> 0. Exactness is verified on representatives by divisibility by y. Module.Finite.of_exact gives the induction step. With n=q and y^q=x this makes T/xT finite.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032P (lemma-tate-japanese, lines 45534-45589), proof: 'Note that S/y^nS has a finite filtration whose subquotients are the modules y^iS/y^{i+1}S ≅ S/yS. Hence we see that each S/y^nS is finite over R. In particular S/xS is finite over R'

proof.text: Write S=integralClosure R L. The inclusion S -> T has inverse image of xT equal to xS. If x has zero image in L both ideals are zero. Otherwise, if a in S maps to xb in T, let c=a/x in L; its image is b. Integrality is reflected by the injective field map, so c is integral over R and lies in S, and a=xc. The induced quotient map S/xS -> T/xT is therefore injective. Noetherianity and finiteness of T/xT give finiteness of S/xS over R. Identify the extended principal ideal with Ideal.span {x} acting on the top R-submodule, and use restriction of scalars to obtain finiteness over R/xR.

For a normal Noetherian domain R and a prime principal ideal xR with Japanese quotient R/xR, the reduction modulo x of the integral closure in a finite purely inseparable extension is a finite module.

lean.statement:
theorem tate_purely_inseparable_closure_quotient_finite
    (R : Type u) (K L : Type v) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K]
    [Algebra K L] [Algebra R L] [IsScalarTower R K L]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] (x : R) (hnormal : IsIntegrallyClosed R)
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP K p] [FiniteDimensional K L]
    [IsPurelyInseparable K L]
    [IsDomain (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({x} : Set R))]
    (hquot : IsN2 (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({x} : Set R))
      (FractionRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({x} : Set R)))) :
    Module.Finite (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({x} : Set R))
      ((integralClosure R L) ⧸
        (Ideal.span ({x} : Set R) • ⊤ : Submodule R (integralClosure R L)))
